title: Runtime Quantization Rollout Operator Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the operator-run steps and automation patterns for safely rolling out model quantization changes in Redwood’s serving runtime. Quantization (INT8/4-bit) can materially reduce cost and increase throughput but carries risk of degraded output quality or unexpected latency/precision regressions. This document codifies preflight checks, canary strategies, observability signals, automated safeties, and rollback criteria.

When to use this playbook

- Deploying a new quantized model version (e.g., v2-int8) to production.
- Switching live routing policy from FP16/FP32 variant to a quantized variant.
- Enabling an automated quantization profile for a model family.

Assumptions and prerequisites

- Model artifacts are stored in the model registry with clear semantic versions and a "quantized" tag.
- Canary clusters/environments exist per region: canary-<region>-small (1–5% traffic).
- Observability hooks exist for token-latency, generation-quality-metrics, and per-tenant cost.
- Rollouts are performed by Platform Operators or SREs with the "platform:operator" role.
- A rollback pipeline and artifact pinning mechanism are available in the deployment orchestration CLI.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: Runtime Performance team (eng-runtime).
- On-call escalation: Platform SRE (pager duty: eng-platform-sre) for production incidents.
- Product/ML contact: model-owner listed on model registry entry.

Pre-deployment checks (automated and manual)

1) CI validation (automated):
   - Unit inference tests pass on quantized artifact (>= 95% of reference logits within tolerance).
   - End-to-end smoke tests for service start, KV cache warmup, and streaming responses.
2) Local perf benchmark:
   - Run the dev benchmark harness: sample_lengths = [16,64,512]. Compare p50/p95 token latency and throughput.
3) Quality validation:
   - Run canonical prompt set evals. Target: no more than 1.5% absolute BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-shift regression on critical prompt set.
4) Safety gates:
   - Confirm audit log and debug sampling toggles are enabled for canary traffic.
   - Confirm automatic prefix-cache-population is compatible with quantized KV layout.

Canary rollout procedure (step-by-step)

1) Register artifact: tag model artifact in registry as "quantized-rollout-<date>-<id>" and update model metadata with owners and rollback pin.
2) Deploy to canary clusters (automated):
   - CLI: rwdctl deploy --model <model>:<quantized-tag> --target canary-<region> --concurrency 2 --circuit open
3) Route traffic: shift 2% of new request traffic to quantized canary for 30 minutes.
4) Monitor baseline metrics (30–60 minutes):
   - Token-level latency: p50, p95, p99.
   - Throughput (tokens/sec) and GPU utilization.
   - Quality signals: semantic-similarity vs baseline (embedding cosine), token distribution drift, hallucination heuristics.
   - Business KPIs: error-rate, per-tenant cost delta, downstream QPS.
5) Expand incrementally if safe: 2% -> 5% -> 15% -> 40% -> 100%. Hold for a minimum observation window at each step (recommended windows: 30m, 60m, 2h, 4h, 12h respectively).

Key observability signals and thresholds

- Latency regressions:
  - p50 increase > 15% OR p95 increase > 25% over baseline -> alert (severity: P2).
  - p99 increase > 40% -> immediate rollback recommendation (P1).
- Quality regressions (canary-vs-baseline on canonical prompts):
  - Semantic-similarity mean drop > 0.03 cosine -> in_review.
  - Failure mode spike (e.g., truncated answers, malformed JSON) > 0.5% absolute -> immediate rollback.
- Error-rate (5xx/streaming disconnects): >= 0.5% absolute increase -> immediate rollback.
- GPU OOM or high CUDA-scheduler preemption events: any occurrence -> immediate pause and investigation.

SLOs and dashboards to watch

Table (text):
| Metric | Canary Threshold (per-step) | Action | Owner |
|-------|---------------------------|--------|-------|
| p95 token latency | +25% vs baseline | Alert P2, investigate | eng-runtime |
| 5xx rate | +0.5% absolute | Rollback candidate | eng-sre |
| Semantic-similarity (mean) | -0.03 | Hold + human eval | model-owner |
| Hallucination heuristic rate | +0.5% absolute | Rollback | eng-runtime |
| GPU OOM events | any | Pause rollout | platform-ops |

Automated safeties and circuit breakers

- Rolling window guard: automated canary controller evaluates metrics; if any hard thresholds hit, controller will automatically revert traffic shift and pin traffic to previous variant.
- Token-cost throttle: if per-tenant per-minute token cost increases beyond configured soft-limit, routing will fall back to FP16 variant for that tenant only.
- Canary lock: only one quantization rollout per model-family per-region active at a time.

Rollback criteria and procedure

Immediate rollback (automated or manual) if any of the following occur during any canary step:
- p99 latency > baseline + 40%
- 5xx rate increase >= 0.5% absolute
- Semantic-similarity drop >= 0.05 or hallucination spike >= 1.0%
- Any GPU OOM or host-level kernel panic

Rollback steps:
1) Trigger automated rollback from controller or run: rwdctl rollout rollback --model <model> --region <region> --from-tag <quantized-tag>
2) Re-pin traffic to previous artifact: rwdctl route pin --model <model> --tag <previous-tag> --region <region>
3) Open an incident (use standard incident template) and notify model owner, eng-runtime, and platform-sre.
4) Collect debug bundle: rwdctl debug collect --canary-id <id> --output /tmp/canary-debug.tgz
5) If rollback was manual, record the decision and return to the pre-deployment checklist before retrying.

Post-rollout validation and clean-up

- Run targeted A/B quality checks for a 24–48 hour period: full canonical prompt set + customer-specific prompt subsets.
- Confirm observability retention: trace spans and sample outputs are stored per retention policy for forensics.
- Remove temporary audit sampling toggles once validated.
- Update model registry with rollout result and attach post-rollout notes.

Postmortem guidance

- If rollback occurred: run a blameless postmortem within 3 business days. Include artifact diffs, sampled outputs, and operator timeline.
- If rollout succeeded: add a short technical note documenting observed benefits (latency/throughput/cost) and any anomalies.

Appendix: example deployment YAML and CLI snippets

Deployment YAML (example):
---
model: my-nlp-model
version: v3-int8
quantization: true
resources:
  replicas: 4
  gpu: nvidia-a100:1
canary_policy:
  region: us-west-2
  steps: [2,5,15,40,100]
  step_windows: [30m,60m,2h,4h,12h]
---

Common CLI snippets:
- Deploy to canary: rwdctl deploy --model my-nlp-model:v3-int8 --target canary-us-west-2 --concurrency 2
- Increase canary traffic: rwdctl route shift --model my-nlp-model --region us-west-2 --pct 5
- Rollback: rwdctl rollout rollback --model my-nlp-model --region us-west-2
- Collect debug bundle: rwdctl debug collect --canary-id 20260215-qa --output /tmp/debug.tgz
